_: Human coronal dentin: ~70 % mineral by weight in a collagen matrix pierced by tubules (density and diameter rising toward the pulp); yellower and less translucent than enamel; the bulk of the tooth under the enamel and in the root. Values for hydrated permanent dentin at room or body temperature. Materials research lane, mouth group, 2026-11-07.

alpha.src: exposed dentin (worn or at the cervix) is less glossy than enamel; not measured

mu_s_per_cm.src: FRIED95 dentin ~260 cm-1 in the visible and near IR (tubules scatter)

colour_Lab_with_enamel_3mm.src: ARDU10 enamel + dentin 3 mm in vivo (via MTT section 4); dentin alone not measured there

translucency.v: lower than enamel: scatters strongly, absorbs weakly in the yellow (organic matrix): the source of tooth body colour

kinetic.src: not found as a clean value; Zheng 2003 (dentin vs titanium in artificial saliva) higher than enamel - numbers not retrieved

restitution.src: not found; tougher, less stiff and more damped than enamel (collagen), so a lower rebound than enamel's 0.85 E

water_contact_angle_deg.src: not found; hydrophilic, tubule fluid wets the cut surface

porosity.v: tubules ~1-2.5 um diameter, ~20-45 % area near the pulp falling to a few % near the DEJ

collision_thickness_mm.src: numerical skin for a rigid solid

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: rigid relative to soft tissue: Hertz with E 22.5 GPa

contact_damping_ratio.src: collagen gives some damping, more than enamel (not measured)

damping_ratio.src: collagen gives some damping, more than enamel (not measured)

deform.model_note: tough, slightly viscoelastic composite; fails with some plasticity

E_GPa.src: KINNEY03 critical review: E 20-25 GPa (older literature uncertain by 3x); TOOTHREV 12-20

poisson.src: nu = E/(2G) - 1 with E 22.5, G 8.5 (KINNEY03 mid values); sensitive to both

toughness_MPa_m05.src: KINNEY03 citing Iwamoto: K_c 1.79 (worst case); TOOTHREV 1.5-2.1; toughness falls with age

viscoelastic.v: measurable creep and stress relaxation from the collagen and tubule fluid (ZHANG14 reviews it)

conductivity_W_mK.src: THERM_T dentin 0.11-0.96 W/mK (older studies; 0.57 a commonly quoted middle value, E within the range)

dehydrated.src: drying stiffens dentin (KINNEY03 discusses the effect); the size here is an estimate

aged_transparent.src: tubules fill with mineral with age: more translucent, more brittle (lower toughness), little change in E (literature summary, values not retrieved)
